title: Anti-NMDAR Encephalitis in a 13-Year-Old Female: A 24-Month Clinical Follow-Up
case_prompt:
A previously healthy 13-year-old girl developed recurrent clonic movements of her right arm and leg lasting about 2 minutes without loss of consciousness, for which she was started on levetiracetam. Two weeks later she presented with right leg weakness, right hand and foot paresthesia, and acute aphasia. On admission she was febrile (38 °C), alert but inarticulate with impaired comprehension, had continuous right arm clonic movements, and exhibited right-sided motor power of 4/5 with paresthesia. Cranial nerves were intact; there was no rash, trauma, or significant past medical history.  
Laboratory studies showed a normal CBC; ANA, RF, immunoglobulins, complement levels, thyroid function, and α-fetoprotein were within normal limits. CSF analysis revealed no pleocytosis or biochemical abnormalities; bacterial and viral cultures were negative. Serum and CSF antibody titers for HSV, enterovirus, and Japanese encephalitis virus were not elevated.  
EEG demonstrated continuous slow waves in the left hemisphere with frequent left temporal spikes and multiple electroclinical seizures. Brain MRI (T2-weighted) showed multifocal high-signal intensity lesions with cortical swelling in bilateral temporal lobes, predominantly on the left, involving the limbic system.  
Empiric therapy with intravenous vancomycin, cefotaxime, acyclovir, azithromycin, dexamethasone, and antiseizure medications was initiated. On hospital day 2, IVIG (400 mg/kg/day for 5 days) was added given concern for limbic and autoimmune encephalitis based on MRI findings.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Acute bacterial meningitis was considered but ruled out — “On the 10th hospital day, antibiotic treatments were ceased because the bacterial cultures exhibited no growth of bacterial organisms.”  
2. Herpes simplex virus encephalitis was suspected but excluded — “Despite the negative polymerase chain reaction results for herpes simplex virus (HSV1 and HSV2), acyclovir was continued for 14 days…”  
3. Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection was considered due to a high titer — “the mycoplasma pneumoniae antibody titer was 1:640.”  
4. Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis was in the differential but unsupported by CSF — “The CSF analysis did not indicate pleocytosis or other biochemical abnormalities…”  
5. Paraneoplastic encephalitis was investigated but no tumor was found — “there was no demonstrable tumorous lesion.”  
6. Anti-NMDAR autoimmune encephalitis was confirmed by CSF antibody testing — “On the 15th hospital day, the CSF tests for autoimmune antibodies revealed the presence of anti-NMDAR antibodies.”
